To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) we propose a novel PrLM, named True-NegPreLM, to train on true negative samples, and (2) we demonstrate its effectiveness by extensive experiments on a wide variety of tasks

(1) the false negative problem exists in discriminative PrLMs, (2) the false negative issue is caused by the lack of true negative data, (3) the false negatives are not randomly distributed but are clustered in some specific regions of the corrupted texts, and (4) the false negative data can be effectively detected by a simple but effective detection algorithm.
we propose a novel PrLM pre-training framework, called True Negatives (TN) PrLM, which can be trained on true negative samples, i.e., the corrupted texts that are not the original ones.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: How to effectively pre-train language models with true negative samples?
how to construct better negative samples to improve the training of discriminative PrLMs and thus to obtain more robust and more efficient PrLMs.
a new type of PrLM, which we call True Negatives Language Model Pre-training (TnLMPT), which is trained on true negative samples.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the false negative issue is the major reason that the discriminative PrLMS are not as good as the generative PrLMS, which is the major reason why the discriminative PrLSMs cannot achieve comparable performance as the generative ones.
the false negatives in PrLMs are a major cause of their poor performance and should be addressed in order to improve their performance.
the existing discriminative PrLMs suffer from the false negatives issue, which is a major drawback for them to achieve a high-quality PrLM.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose a novel framework to pre-train language models on both positive and negative data, which can be trained effectively by using a novel true negative mining algorithm to mine true negatives from corrupted texts, and thus the resulting PrLM can achieve better contextual representation and better robustness.
we propose a new pre-training framework for discriminative PrLMs by introducing a novel negative sampling strategy that can effectively filter out the false negatives.
we propose to pre-train language models on both positive and negative samples, but we do not treat the negative samples as the same.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quality of negative samples can be improved by examining the corrupted texts and filtering out the true negatives.
we should not treat all negative samples equally, and instead should distinguish the quality of the negative samples.

, in addition to the positive samples, we should also construct true negative samples to further improve the performance of the resulting PrLM, and this can be done by using an external language model to filter out the corrupted texts.
